title: HOKA Val d'Aran by UTMB 2027 — VDA race page, track and time chart
publisher: HOKA Val d'Aran by UTMB / UTMB World Series
claims: The 2027 event runs from 7 to 11 July 2027; the VDA starts on Friday 9 July 2027 at 16:00 from Vielha and finishes back in Vielha.
The 2027 VDA is 163 km with 10,000 m of positive gain and a maximum allowed race time of 48 hours.

The event presents eight race formats and describes VDA, CDH and PDA as the 100M, 100K and 50K equivalents in the UTMB World Series finals pathway, with direct finals access for the top 10 men and women in each.
The 2027 CDH is 110 km with 6,400 m of positive gain, starts in Les at 06:00 on Friday 9 July 2027 and has a 28-hour limit.
The 2027 TDL is 75 km with 5,100 m of positive gain, starts in Bossòst at 07:30 on Wednesday 7 July 2027 and has a 20-hour limit.
The 2027 PDA is 55 km with 3,300 m of positive gain and 3,700 m of negative gain, starts in Salardú at 07:00 on Thursday 8 July 2027 and has a 14-hour limit.
The 2027 EXP is 32 km with 2,100 m of gain, starts in Vielha at 08:00 on Sunday 11 July 2027 and has a limit of 7 hours 15 minutes.
The 2027 SKY is 18 km with 900 m of gain, starts at Pla de Beret at 09:30 on Saturday 10 July 2027 and has a 4-hour limit.
The event also lists an 18 km SKY Promesas and a 10 km Vielha 10K; the home page gives the 10K 500 m of gain while the 2026 race report gives 600 m.
The embedded VDA track totals 163.011 km with 10,053 m of positive gain, 10,049 m of negative gain, a maximum elevation of 2,551 m and a minimum of 609 m.

The track lists 27 points, including 16 intermediate timed checkpoints at cumulative distances of 10.5, 21.0, 32.8, 42.6, 49.2, 58.2, 65.8, 81.8, 99.7, 104.8, 113.7, 122.6, 134.2, 144.5, 149.0 and 154.9 km, with the finish at 163.0 km.

Cut-offs are published at 14 intermediate points and the finish: Bassa d'Oles Friday 19:15, Artiga de Lin 21:15, Portilhon Saturday 04:00, Bossòst 05:30, Canejan 08:00, Refugi Honeria 09:15, Còth de Varradòs 16:00, Montgarri 20:45, Beret 22:15, Salardú Sunday 00:00, Banhs de Tredòs 02:45, Colomèrs 07:00, Arties 10:45, Stet Escunhau 13:15 and Vielha Sunday 16:00; Poilaner and Mont-Romies have no cut-off.

The Slowest column is later than the published cut-off at Refugi Honeria, Còth de Varradòs, Montgarri, Beret, Salardú, Banhs de Tredòs, Colomèrs, Arties and the finish, while at the earlier cut-off points the Slowest is earlier than the cut-off.
VDA runners receive three 30-litre bags, delivered to Bossòst, Salardú and Arties; the bags are returned to Vielha and must be collected within two hours of the runner's finish.
Assistance is allowed only at Bossòst, Salardú and Arties, by one person with a bag of at most 30 litres; pacers are not allowed.
The mandatory equipment is published as a downloadable PDF; the race page does not reproduce the list in text.

The tracks page links to a file named VDA_2027_COLOMERS_...gpx, but the downloaded file's metadata names it 'VDA 2026_COLOMERS', gives gpx.studio as author, a creation time of 2024-05-30 and Strava route links, and carries no licence or copyright terms.
The race page's embedded gpxUrl points to a file named VDA_2026_WEB_COLOMERS_...gpx.
The highest named point on the track is Pòrt d'Urets at 2,520 m; the highest timed checkpoint is Còth de Varradòs at 2,048 m; the track maximum of 2,551 m is higher than both.
The UTMB World Series event list embedded in the same site marks Val d'Aran by UTMB as a Major (isMajor 1) in Europe, Spain, with dates 7–11 July 2027.

The race page describes the VDA as 'Torn dera Val d'Aran, the tour of the Val d'Aran', '163 kilometres of demanding terrain', crossing 'wild valleys, abandoned mines and cirques of lakes' and the Aranese culture.

The track's 27 points are named, in order, VIELHA, Tuc Montcorbison, BASSA D'OLES, ARTIGA DE LIN, Uelhs deth Joeu, Tuc dera Escaleta, POILANER, Còth de Baretja, PORTILHON, BOSSÒST, Les, CANEJAN, REFUGI HONERIA, Mines de Liat, CÒTH DE VARRADÒS, Pòrt d'Urets, MONTGARRI, BERET, SALARDÚ, BANHS DE TREDÒS, Estanh Obago, COLOMÈRS, MONT-ROMIES, ARTIES, STET ESCUNHAU, Tuc de Meddia and VIELHA.
The track's cutoffDatetime values carry the years 2022 (14 points) and 2023 (Stet Escunhau), while the displayed cutoff text uses the 2027 weekdays.
The track's supplies field marks 11 points as food, 3 as hotFood (Bossòst, Salardú, Arties) and 3 as drink (Poilaner, Mont-Romies, Stet Escunhau); the remaining points are none.

The track records per-point facilities: Artiga de Lin has toilets and a bus; Bossòst has toilets, a bus, a rest area and a bag drop; Canejan, Refugi Honeria, Montgarri, Beret, Salardú, Banhs de Tredòs, Colomèrs and Arties have toilets (Beret, Salardú, Banhs de Tredòs and Arties also a bus); Salardú and Arties have a rest area and a bag drop; the finish has toilets, a bag drop and showers.

Checkpoint altitudes along the track are 1,600, 1,185, 2,000, 1,292, 710, 891, 1,017, 2,048, 1,659, 1,850, 1,260, 1,759, 1,980, 1,765, 1,139 and 1,780 m at the 16 intermediate checkpoints, with the finish at 982 m; the non-timed point Les is at 640 m.
Every point on the track carries the difficulty label T3.
